definition: Expound means to lay out a subject in full, careful detail — to explain it thoroughly and at length, often with 'on' or 'upon.'
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word expound. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know expound should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Give the ferry captain one question about the tides and he will expound for the whole crossing, charting currents on a napkin by the time you dock.
Outlining is weaker than expounding: an outline hands you the skeleton in five bullet points, while to expound is to build the whole body of the subject in front of the audience.
Anatomize goes further than expound: expounding lays a subject out generously, but to anatomize is to dissect it down to every last joint and fiber, sparing the listener nothing.

Elaborate (on) means to add more detail to something already said — a follow-up move that fills in a picture the audience has seen. Expound is the full performance from the start: setting out the whole subject, part by part, at length.

Explain simply makes something understandable, and a good explanation can take one sentence. Expound is explanation gone long-form — thorough, ordered, and usually delivered by someone with a whole theory to lay out.

At the reunion, somebody asked the retired engineer how the old mill dam had actually worked, and she expounded happily for an hour: sluice gates, load curves, the winter the ice nearly won — a full course delivered over cooling coffee.
One fact would have answered the question; she instead set out the whole architecture, system by system, with evident command.
That thorough, extended laying-out of a subject is what expound names — explanation at full length and full dress.
Expound belongs to lecterns, long answers, and people glad you asked.
Its unit-mate explicate unpacks a particular text or problem, piece by piece; expound sets out the speaker's own subject or doctrine at length.
Keep it clear of the look-alike expand (to grow in size) and of its root-cousin propound: you propound a theory in a sentence and expound it for an hour.

Ask a polite question about tomatoes and she will expound on the entire underground economy of a garden: fungi trading sugar for phosphorus, worms turning the subsoil, bacteria pulling nitrogen out of thin air.
Each player gets its chapter, in order, with a jar of soil passed around as the exhibit.
Listeners who wanted a quick tip sometimes edge away.

By closing time, a question that could have been answered with 'add compost' has become an hour-long tour of everything happening under a garden bed.
